Always stamp your plots with script name

Source: R/ggstamp.R
ggstamp.Rd

This function is used to stamp ggplot type plots with datetime and script name. User must provide the script name.

Usage

ggstamp(
  plot,
  file,
  size,
  script,
  time,
  model,
  stamp.gg.style,
  stamp.format = NULL,
  stamp.funs = NULL
)

Arguments

plot

The plot to be stamped.

file

An optional output filename to be included in the stamp.

size

The size (list) for the plot, not the caption. Used to calculate the size of the caption.

script

the script name. Date and time will be added automatically.

time

The timestamp to be included.

model

An optional model name or object to be included in the stamp.

stamp.gg.style

A list of formatting options for the stamp text. For ggplot objects, valid elements include size, colour, hjust, vjust, and other parameters accepted by ggplot2::element_text(). For gtable objects, valid elements include col, fill, alpha, lty, lwd, lex, lineend, linejoin, linemitre, fontsize, cex, fontfamily, fontface, lineheight, and font. Default formatting is applied if not specified. Additionally, the element position controls where the stamp is placed: "left", "center", "right" (default) or a number between 0 (left) and 1 (right). hjust controls justification of the lines within the stamp and defaults to 0 (left-justified). Example: stamp.gg.style=list(position="right",hjust=0) places the stamp on the right with left-justified lines.

stamp.format

A template for the stamp text using the placeholders %script, %time, %model, and %file, with "\n" for line breaks. Default is "%file\n%script\n%model\n%time". See createStamp.

stamp.funs

Optional named list of functions (elements script, time, model, file) used to preprocess the values before they are inserted into stamp.format. See createStamp.

Value

A stamped plot object. If size is given, a patchwork object with the stamp panel underneath the plot. Otherwise the plot with the stamp added as caption. For gtable input, a gtable. If plot is a list, a list of stamped plots.

Details

The stamp text is generated by createStamp based on stamp.format and stamp.funs. If the plot already has a caption, the stamp is added below it.

How the stamp is added depends on size:

  • If size is given (always the case when called from ggwrite), the stamp is drawn in a separate panel underneath the plot (combined using patchwork). The panel height is calculated from the number of stamp lines and the font size, and the plot height is reduced accordingly so the total size matches size. Placement of the stamp (stamp.gg.style$position) and justification of its lines (stamp.gg.style$hjust) are controlled independently.

  • If size is not given, the stamp is added as the plot caption (labs(caption=...)) and styled using theme(plot.caption=...). In this case, hjust controls both placement and justification.

For gtable objects (e.g. from gridExtra::arrangeGrob), the stamp is added at the bottom using arrangeGrob.

ggplot 2.2.1 or newer is required.

See also

Other Plotting: canvasSize(), ggwater(), ggwrite()

Examples

library(ggplot2)
data(ChickWeight)
p1 <- ggplot(ChickWeight,aes(Time,weight,group=Chick,colour=factor(Diet)))+geom_line()
script <- "note"
ggstamp(p1,script)

## Or use ggwrite which will call ggstamp when the `script` argument is provided.
ggwrite(p1,script=script,canvas="wide")
